timeline_reviews.summary: Transport trajectory records the parent turn from start through final answer, including spawned work, commands, file changes, and closure.
Parent probed the binary, spawned plural and case probes, wrote the main Rust project, fixed a Rust type error, built and tested, waited on children, interrupted one, and finalized.
Plural probe child ran black-box noun and case probes, including empty and non-ASCII checks, and returned a compact behavior report used by the parent.
Case child spawned a nested probe, also wrote an alternate Cargo scaffold into /output, detected divergence from another writer, cleaned duplicate files, rebuilt, tested, then was interrupted.
Nested case probe explored camelize, underscore, classify, tableize, delimiter, casing, and composition behavior and returned a detailed report.

Single serial actor probed the C++ executable, implemented the Cargo project and modules, built release, diffed representative and edge cases, copied the binary, and finalized.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for a pure Rust 2021 black-box port, same CLI loop over up to four args, exact stdout, no external crates, root test12.rs, and Cargo-compatible module organization.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while spawning probe_plural and probe_case; probe_case spawned a nested case probe and also began its own implementation, creating overlapping ownership of /output files.
parallel.implementation: The final implementation used naive +s pluralization, trailing-s singularization, underscore-driven camelize, uppercase-driven underscore, composed classify/tableize, humanize, dasherize, upcase, and downcase.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The delivered tree contained Cargo metadata, root test12.rs, src/lib.rs, and src/inflection modules; a child-parent shared-write collision was reconciled before final delivery.
parallel.verification: The run executed cargo build, cargo test, direct rustc builds, comparison scripts against the C++ binary, empty-argument checks, and then passed the official 40/40 evaluator.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No functional task defect remained; the residual issue was process-level shared-output instability and an interrupted child after the final solution path was already working.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same pure Rust, std-only, black-box, byte-for-byte output, same CLI argument behavior, root test12.rs, and modular Cargo project requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor performed probing, implementation, build, comparison, binary copy, and final response without delegation or shared ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial solution implemented Inflector with number, case, and composition helpers matching the observed simple behavior of the compiled C++ executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial tree had a coherent Cargo package, root test12.rs, src/inflection modules, and copied release binary at /output/test12.
serial.verification: The serial actor built release and ran multiple diff comparisons against the C++ binary, including examples, empty strings, repeated underscores, uppercase endings, and composition-sensitive cases, then passed 40/40 officially.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task-relevant defect or coordination issue was visible at closure; the serial control remained non-delegated and passed all official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel tracked the prompt requirements for pure Rust, std-only behavior, exact CLI/output matching, root test12.rs, and black-box probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial tracked the same prompt requirements and used the same compiled executable as the behavioral oracle.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference; both solved the same accepted black-box port obligation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed probing into child agents while the parent retained implementation; one child also attempted implementation in the shared output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor for probing, implementation, verification, binary copy, and closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created overlapping output ownership while serial kept a single implementation owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel exchanged probe findings through child reports, including a plural report consumed by the parent and nested case findings within the child path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all findings in the same actor context and did not need cross-agent briefs, contracts, or handoff reduction.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Handoffs were generally usable, but parallel had weaker shared-output boundaries than serial because a child moved from probing into direct implementation without a stable file ownership contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent wrote the final modular implementation, fixed the ASCII mapping compile error, and matched the nonstandard binary behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a modular implementation once, built it, and did not require cross-agent reconciliation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementations converged on the same simple transform rules, but parallel had an intermediate alternate scaffold and repair path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received the plural probe report, timed out on waits for remaining child activity, listed agents, and interrupted the still-running probe_case child after the solution path was working.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all results stayed in the main trajectory and final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra child wait/interruption lifecycle overhead, but it did not leave a required result unjoined for the final solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had a direct shared-state incident: parent and child wrote overlapping root deliverable and project files, after which the child saw divergence and cleaned stale files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the output tree through one actor and copied the release binary to the root without concurrent writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main process difference: parallel had deliverable overwrite/reconciliation, while serial had a linear final tree lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran cargo build, cargo test, direct rustc builds, comparisons against the C++ executable, empty-argument checks, and passed official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran cargo build and diff comparisons against representative and edge cases, then passed official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had adequate acceptance evidence; parallel verification included extra repair/recheck after the shared-write episode.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents, 89 LLM requests, more tool calls, and 262 agent seconds, but completed within budget and passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, 21 LLM requests, fewer tool calls, and 174 agent seconds, and also passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent substantially more coordination budget for no outcome gain on this task, with one retained adverse write episode; serial was simpler and faster but equally correct.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records show both modes passed 40/40, so there is no discordant official outcome. The concrete solution difference is process-level: the parallel run used probes and suffered a shared deliverable overwrite that it repaired, while the serial run completed the same black-box implementation linearly.
parallel_contributors: Child probes supplied useful black-box behavior evidence, especially plural/case details.
A child-parent shared output write episode caused reconciliation work but did not survive as a functional defect.
serial_contributors: Single-thread probing and implementation avoided cross-agent write boundaries.
Serial verification covered examples and edge cases before copying the binary.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel briefly had an ASCII mapping type error that was fixed before final verification.
Parallel left an extra standalone rustc-built binary name in the artifact listing, but the official expected entry and executable were accepted.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process episode only

candidates.reason: Parallel had an active parent implementation owner and even an overzealous child implementer; the issue was overlapping ownership, not absence of an implementer.
Integration was not left unowned: the final tree was reconciled and built after the overlapping writes.
The required root entry file and binaries were assembled in `/output`; the problem was replacement of that entry, not lack of an assembly owner.
Implementation, build, comparison, and delivery all occurred; no end-to-end transition was ownerless.
Binary probing happened early, but productive implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial gate with an unfinished or shortened closure consequence.
The run overlapped child probing with parent implementation and child implementation activity; it was not an all-investigation phase followed by deadline-constrained production.
The indispensable implementation path received capacity and completed; no auxiliary work starved the critical path.
Although several agents were spawned and one spawn hit a live-agent limit, the run did not exhaust the time budget or lose required work before closure.
No single child received an overbroad indispensable assignment that remained unfinished; the adverse event was shared deliverable writing.
The visible child work probed the intended black-box behavior and produced usable findings or artifacts; no known parent requirement is shown missing from a brief and causing unusable work.
There were no separately delegated components whose omitted API contract made them incompatible; the directly evidenced problem was same deliverable replacement.
No known finding disappeared between actors; the useful plural probe result was returned to the parent and used.
Returned probe reports were long but were not left materially unconsumed because of their size; final verification still succeeded.
No actor is shown consuming a superseded report as current truth; the stale state was a shared workspace write collision, not a handoff.
No incompatible child reports remained unadjudicated at a decision point; workspace divergence was reconciled by cleanup and rebuild.
The parent did not merely assume completion from file existence: it ran builds and output comparisons, and the current official evaluation passed 40/40.
There was no replacement child or retry that repeated prior work without inherited findings; ordinary command failures were corrected locally.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: A child was interrupted, but the needed implementation and verification were already available through the shared tree; no indispensable child result was stopped before it could be used.
A usable candidate was not left unpromoted; the final project and executable were present before closure.
The cleanup after overlapping writes was followed by rebuild/test activity and later parent checks, so this was not an unverified post-check merge.
The child implementation was not a completed separate artifact that the parent failed to retrieve; it landed in the shared workspace and is covered by the write label.
No verifier child produced a trapped required finding; visible probe results either returned or were superseded by direct verification.
The interrupted child did not leave an unhandled required failure scope; the parent and shared workspace reached a passing implementation.
The parent consumed the plural probe result, and no ignored completed result is shown to make the final state inconsistent.
The parent had a timed wait, but it also inspected agent state and continued with local verification; no deadline failure resulted from blind waiting.
Overlapping implementation ownership existed, but the same root deliverable file was replaced, making Deliverable Overwrite more specific.
Same-file collision is a near match, but replacement of the required entry-point source is directly evidenced and takes precedence.
Some non-entry source cleanup occurred, but the same episode includes replacement of the root entry deliverable, so Source Overwrite is not the narrowest label.

A child wrote the root `test12.rs` deliverable and Cargo scaffold, the parent later wrote overlapping root deliverable files while the child was still active, and the child observed divergence and performed cleanup/rebuild.
candidates.realized_consequence: The overlapping writes forced reconciliation of a replaced root entry-point source and stale duplicate files before the final parallel tree could be trusted.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-file editing is present, but the affected file was the required root entry deliverable, so Deliverable Overwrite is the more specific taxonomy child.

candidates.reason: There was no broad final-tree promotion or cleanup that replaced multiple current outputs; the specific event centers on the root deliverable and adjacent source files.
Shared unisolated writes caused a provenance problem, but a more specific deliverable overwrite is proven for the same episode.
No temporary artifact, cache, fixture, or auxiliary tool from one actor was consumed by another as a reference environment.

retained_patterns.reason: A child wrote the root entry-point source and Cargo scaffold in `/output`; while that child was still active, the parent wrote overlapping root deliverable files, after which the child detected divergent `/output/test12.rs` state and cleaned/rebuilt. Serial had one writer for the same deliverable path.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The deliverable replacement created unstable provenance and forced a cleanup/rebuild pass before the final parallel output tree was coherent.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The episode includes same-file conflict, but the overwritten file was the required root entry source, so the deliverable-specific child is the canonical retained label.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Same-File Collision, Source Overwrite, Cross-File Scope Collision, and Unisolated Workspace Writes were suppressed for the same shared-output episode because Deliverable Overwrite is the most specific applicable write label.
Early Child Termination and Blind Timeout Wait were not retained because the interrupted/waited child chain did not leave indispensable work unfinished after the deliverable overwrite was repaired.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; only the direct shared deliverable replacement had a realized adverse process consequence.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The retained episode was not split into additional ownership, timing, or lower-precedence write labels because those would reuse the same anchors and consequence.
